alignments.note: The *It* of *It was but a little* is a cleft/impersonal dummy, not the presentative *there* rule 20 hands to a predicate, so no morpheme licenses it and it is its own added unit under rule 30. This is the correction: the accepted alignment folded it into מְעַט's unit alongside the copula.
Approximative כְּ of כִּמְעַט rendered by the restrictive *but*; the alternative fuses כְּ with מְעַט under rule 30, but the ASV spends separate English on each, so rule 2 splits them.

Predicate of the verbless clause: it carries the construction-supplied copula *was* (rule 20) and the supplied indefinite article *a* (rule 15), discontinuous around *but* under rule 25. The dummy *It* is excluded, since rule 20's construction-supplied frame reaches the presentative *there* and no other.
Relative שֶׁ → *that*.
Finite verb with its subject pronoun; head on the lexical verb (rules 17, 24).
מִן → *from*.
Suffix → *them* (rule 18).
עַד plus its relative rendered by the single word *When*, which carries both the temporal relation and the subordination (rule 30); head on עַד, the morpheme carrying the temporal content (rule 23).
Finite verb with subject pronoun.
Object marker H853 with no English of its own (rule 16).
Written relative with its supplied antecedent *him* (rule 46's first rider); head on *whom*, which realizes the relative itself.
אָהֵב → *loveth*; the explicit subject נַפְשִׁי takes its own English.
נֶפֶשׁ → *soul*.
1cs suffix → *my*.
Finite verb with subject pronoun.
Object suffix → *him*.
Waw → *and* (rule 14).
The ASV writes the negation and the modal as two words, so rule 35 splits them and the negative takes only *not*.

Hiphil of רָפָה rendered *would let ... go*, discontinuous around *not* and the object pronoun (rule 25); head on the complement verb *go* by rule 44's second-verb clause, though heading on *let* as a phrasal verb is defensible.

Anarthrous substantival participle as nomen rectum: it carries the chain's *of* (rule 19) together with the supplied *her that* (rule 46), headed on the word carrying the lexeme.

review_notes: Corrected: the *It* of *It was but a little* is split off as its own added unit under rule 20's cleft/impersonal sentence, which reaches the presentative *there* and no other dummy; the copula *was* stays with the predicate מְעַט together with its supplied *a*.

Both עַד + שֶׁ pairs are read as single-word fusions under rule 30, since the ASV writes one word (*When*, *Until*) carrying both the temporal relation and the subordination; each heads on עַד under rule 23.

כִּמְעַט is split: *but* to the preposition and *was ... a little* to the noun, the copula and the indefinite article joining the predicate under rules 20 and 15. The competing reading fuses the pair under rule 30, but the ASV spends separate English on each morpheme.
*would let ... go* heads on *go* under rule 44's second-verb clause; heading on *let* as a phrasal verb remains defensible.
